subject: Migration economics: step-down credits and burst pool sizing for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@acmepayments.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Payments Procurement <procurement@acmepayments.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: credits and burst pool question

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the overview last week. We are evaluating a move from your hosted API to a Reserved (Dedicated) pool for production. Two areas we need clarity on before we take this to procurement:

1) Conversion credits: our finance team wants a clear amortization schedule that offsets revenue impact during the first 6 months of commitment. Can you outline a staged credit schedule (front-loaded vs taper) and whether credits apply to token usage or to the committed monthly invoice?

2) Burst / temporary capacity: we run predictable spikes (quarterly settlement and occasional promos). If we reserve X GPUs, what's the short-term burst capacity policy? Any priced burst months or temporary pool add-ons we can rely on while we finish sizing?

3) Throughput guarantee: we need a SLT on p99 token latency and a defined remediation path (credits or additional capacity) if you miss the throughput buckets.

Attached a short requirements note (acme_requirements.pdf). Would like a written proposal we can share with procurement by next week.

- Andrew
Acme Payments

Attachments: acme_requirements.pdf (document stub)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: credits and burst pool question

Hi Andrew — thanks for the clear ask and the requirements doc. High level answers below; I attached a draft proposal (acme_proposal_v3.pdf) with numbers you can share with procurement.

1) Conversion credits: we propose a 6-month staged credit schedule tied to the committed monthly invoice. Mechanics:
- Months 1–2: 100% conversion credit applied to your committed spend (credit reduces invoice)
- Months 3–4: 50% conversion credit
- Months 5–6: 25% conversion credit
Credits are applied to the monthly Reserved invoice, not per-token billing, to keep bookkeeping aligned with the contract. We can discuss an accelerated taper if you want shorter coverage in exchange for a larger up-front commit.

2) Burst / temporary capacity: proposal includes a 2-month shared burst pool (no instant hardware provisioning). You get a defined burst allowance (measured in token-minutes or vGPU-hours depending on workload) priced at a reduced incremental rate during the first 3 transition months. If you need on-demand physical capacity immediately, we can offer a paid short-term GPU add-on (priced separately) with 72‑hour provisioning SLA.

3) Throughput guarantees: we can commit to p99 token generation latency targets for the primary model family within the committed pool. Remedies: if p99 SLA is missed for >3 consecutive days in a calendar month, you may elect a credit equal to X% of that month's Reserved fee (numbers in the attached proposal).

As a next step, can we schedule a 30‑minute call with Karthik to lock GPU sizing assumptions (token distribution, seq length, concurrency) and Ben to confirm commercial tie‑offs? Our team is available Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: acme_proposal_v3.pdf (pricing + credit schedule)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: credits and burst pool question

Priya / Andrew — adding a few technical constraints to the proposal so the burst pool and throughput guarantees are realistic:

- Sizing guidance (see attached gpu_sizing_sheet.xlsx): for your reported peak token/second budgets and 24h weighting, we recommend a base pool of 8 vGPUs (A100-class equivalent) for steady state and a burst allowance that maps to +3 vGPUs for up to 48 hours per quarter. If you prefer smaller GPUs but more instances we can produce an alternate map.

- Measurement windows: p99 token latency will be measured per model and per-region with a 15-minute rolling window. We exclude client-side network jitter and cold-starts that exceed 5s when a new container is provisioned.

- Cache and batching: to hit the cost numbers in the proposal we strongly recommend enabling prefix KV caching and a service-side batching policy. If you use very long sequences (>4k tokens), effective throughput will drop and we should reassess the vGPU count.

- Fallbacks: our recommended remediation is automatic routing to a compatible hosted variant for shortfalls under 6 hours; beyond that we trigger the contractual credit. The hosted fallback will have reduced throughput per dollar but keeps critical flows alive.

Let me know what concurrency profiles we should assume on the call.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: gpu_sizing_sheet.xlsx (sizing map + assumptions)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: credits and burst pool question

Andrew — thanks for the thoughtful questions and Karthik for the technical breakdown. Priya and I refined pricing and final mechanics in the attached proposal. Summary tweaks:

- Finalized credit schedule: months 1–2 (100%), month 3 (75%), month 4 (50%), month 5 (25%), month 6 (0%). We front-load more credit in month 3 to help your cashflow while still encouraging timely sizing.
- Burst buffer: included 2 paid burst months at a reduced uplift (25% of standard incremental vGPU rate) for the first 6 months. Additional ad‑hoc add-ons are available at our near-term provisioning rate.
- Commit tiers and discounts: 12‑month reserved commit at Tier 2 (10% off list) with an option to step up to Tier 1 (15% off) if you increase committed GPU hours by 40% during month 3.
- Acceptance flow: we can send a DocuSign for the SOW + payment schedule once you confirm the final vGPU count. If procurement approves this week we can target a February 1 start.

Link to execute: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/ACME-2026-proposal
Requested next items from Acme: PO number, preferred billing entity, and preferred start date. Lauren is looped for billing and onboarding logistics.

If the proposal looks good, Priya — please trigger DocuSign and I'll route to Finance for the initial invoice hold.

Best,
Ben Carter
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments: acme_mra_draft.docx (SOW draft)
